overview: Ventricular tachycardia is a potentially life-threatening arrhythmia originating from the ventricles. It is characterized by a ventricular rate typically greater than 100 beats per minute and may significantly impair cardiac output. Episodes may be nonsustained, terminating spontaneously within 30 seconds, or sustained, lasting more than 30 seconds or causing hemodynamic compromise. Sustained ventricular tachycardia may progress to ventricular fibrillation, cardiac arrest, and sudden death.
ecg_clues: very broad qrs greater than 160 ms
uniform qrs morphology in monomorphic vt
rsr pattern with taller left rabbit ear
ecg_limitations: single lead recordings may miss diagnostic vt features
differentiation from svt with aberrancy may be difficult
ecg alone cannot determine structural heart disease severity
ecg alone cannot determine ischemic burden
ecg alone cannot determine long term prognosis
risk_factors: family history of sudden cardiac death

history_questions: Have you experienced episodes of rapid heartbeat?
Do you have chest pain during episodes?
Have you had a previous heart attack?
Have you been diagnosed with heart failure?
Do you have a family history of sudden cardiac death?
Have you been diagnosed with long QT syndrome?

followup_questions.syncope: Have you fainted or lost consciousness recently?
followup_questions.chest_pain: Do you experience chest pain during these episodes?
followup_questions.history_of_mi: Have you had a heart attack before?
followup_questions.coronary_artery_disease: Have you been diagnosed with coronary artery disease?
followup_questions.heart_failure: Have you been diagnosed with heart failure?
followup_questions.cardiomyopathy: Have you been diagnosed with cardiomyopathy?
followup_questions.family_history_sudden_death: Has anyone in your family died suddenly from a heart condition?
followup_questions.long_qt: Have you been diagnosed with long QT syndrome?

confidence_rules: three or more consecutive ventricular beats increase vt confidence
wide qrs greater than 120 ms increases confidence
qrs greater than 160 ms strongly increases confidence
agent_reasoning_hints: treat wide complex tachycardia as VT until proven otherwise
sustained vt lasting more than 30 seconds is a medical emergency
underlying structural heart disease significantly increases risk
previous myocardial infarction significantly increases likelihood
vt may deteriorate into ventricular fibrillation
vt combined with syncope indicates high risk
source_notes: Nonsustained VT lasts less than 30 seconds and terminates spontaneously
Sustained VT lasts more than 30 seconds or causes hemodynamic compromise
VT may progress to ventricular fibrillation
Previous myocardial infarction is one of the most common causes of VT
Capture beats strongly support VT diagnosis
Fusion beats strongly support VT diagnosis
If uncertain between VT and SVT with aberrancy, VT should be assumed until proven otherwise
QRS duration greater than 160 ms strongly favors VT
